description: Size budgets for the payload that ships from apps/mobile. Enforced by scripts/check-mobile-size.mjs on every pull request that touches apps/mobile/**; see .github/workflows/mobile.yml.
notes: Sizes are measured from the output of `npm run size:export` (`expo export`), which is what the installed app actually loads: one Hermes/JS bundle per platform plus the bundled assets.

`expo export` is not bit-for-bit reproducible. Measured on the same tree, the web bundle is byte-identical between runs but Hermes emits .hbc bytecode whose size can shift by tens of bytes run to run. Budgets are therefore set a few percent above the recorded baseline in mobile-baseline.json, never a few bytes above it.

Keep the export output directory (dist/) out of the project listing while measuring - a previous export left inside apps/mobile is picked up as an asset and inflates the next run. dist/ is gitignored for the same reason.
`assets` covers everything in the export that is not a per-platform JS bundle: fonts, images, index.html and the export metadata.
`total` is the sum of the three platform bundles plus `assets`.

Native binary sizes (.aab/.ipa) are not covered by these budgets because producing them needs a full native build. Record one with `npm run size:record-binary -- android=path/to/app.aab`; it is stored under `binary` in mobile-baseline.json.

`warningBytes` reports a non-blocking warning; `maxBytes` fails the pull request. Values are deliberately duplicated per metric rather than derived from a single percentage so that a metric with a known reason to grow (for example a new asset-heavy screen) can be given explicit headroom without loosening every other budget.
